evals.prompt: use clerk-swift to add clerk sign in to my swiftui app (MyApp.xcodeproj). clerk isn't installed yet
evals.expected_output: Sets up Clerk through the iOS setup prompt first, which runs the Clerk CLI, then returns to place sign-in UI; does not ask for a publishable key or install the package by hand
expectations: Follows the iOS setup prompt at https://clerk.com/docs/ios/getting-started/quickstart.md before any UI work
Does NOT ask the user to paste a publishable key
Does NOT add the clerk-ios package, capabilities, or Associated Domains by hand when the CLI can set up the project
Mentions the manual quickstart (?manual=1) only as a fallback when the CLI can't set up the project
Asks for or confirms prebuilt vs custom before implementing sign-in UI

evals.prompt: my ios app already has clerk set up with ClerkKit and Clerk.configure. add the prebuilt sign in sheet
evals.expected_output: Skips setup, adds the ClerkKitUI product only if it's missing, and presents AuthView in a sheet from UserButton signed-out content, keeping the existing configuration
expectations: Does NOT rerun setup or follow the iOS setup prompt again
Adds the ClerkKitUI product only if it isn't already linked, without changing the clerk-ios version requirement
Uses UserButton with signedOutContent to open AuthView() in a .sheet
Keeps the existing Clerk.configure call unchanged
Does NOT call /v1/environment or audit the quickstart

evals.prompt: build a custom sign in flow for my macos swiftui app. clerk is already configured and the publishable key is read from Info.plist through a build setting
evals.expected_output: Builds a multi-step custom flow on ClerkKit that mirrors AuthView, gates steps at runtime from the injected Clerk instance's environment (@Environment(Clerk.self)), and preserves the app's Info.plist key loading
expectations: Keeps the existing Info.plist and build-setting key loading; does NOT hardcode a publishable key
Gates identifiers, factors, and required fields at runtime from the injected Clerk instance's environment instead of hardcoding instance settings
Splits the flow into multiple steps and files that mirror ClerkKitUI AuthView progression
Uses the native Clerk Apple path for Sign in with Apple rather than generic OAuth
